text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on your palms appear as thickened, hyperpigmented skin, and have you noticed any swelling of the lymph nodes in your groin or armpits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any sores or ulcers on your hands, feet, or genitals, and have you experienced any fever or night sweats? REQUEST TEST: Dark_field_microscopy_of_lesions

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical triad of palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, peripheral neuropathy, and madarosis (eyebrow/eyelash loss) is highly suggestive of Hansen's disease. REQUEST TEST: Acid-fast_bacilli_stain_of_skin_biopsy
